CT of the chest reveals an obstructing mass and resultant LUL collapse.
Contrast enhanced chest CT shows diffuse increased interstitial markings involving the right middle and lower lobes.
The prostate is enlarged with several calcifications  noted within.  No dominant prostate mass is evident.
Bladder is prominent with mildly thickened wall. There is a small posteriolateral diverticulum on the rightward aspect.
1.6 x 1.8cm right middle lobe nodule, adjacent/anterior to the medial segment bronchus.
Coronal reconstruction of the axial non-contrast chest CT demonstrates a diffusely dilated esophagus filled with mottled soft tissue consistent with ingested food material.

Large soft tissue mass arising from left adrenal gland measuring 9.5 X 8.9 X 13cm in the oblique coronal, AP, and Craniocaudal dimensions.  Loss of tissue plane between tail of pancreas, spleen, and bowel.
CT (3mm collimation) shows peripheral interlobular septal thickening with scattered focal consolidation and GGO.

Multiple axial CT images of the chest with intravenous contrast material demonstrates a Stanford type A thoracic aortic dissection, with a clear intimal flap separating the true and false lumens of the ascending aorta.  Additionally, a pericardial effusion is noted suspicious for hemopericardium.
